relations.definition: Indicates the target of a penalty or obligation.
relations.embedding_query_text: imposed_on: Indicates the target of a penalty or obligation.

chosen_property.label: imposedOn
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the entity on which a penalty or obligation is imposed.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property expresses the target of a penalty; minting new property.

candidates.label: target
candidates.comment: A destination relation between an action and its intended entry point or URL. Also called "action destination", "target URL", "entry point for action", "leads to". Examples: "The search action has target a search results page", "The button's target is a specific URL", "This action points to a target entry point."

candidates.label: earlyPrepaymentPenalty
candidates.comment: An early prepayment penalty relation between a repayment specification and a monetary amount, representing the fee for paying off a loan ahead of schedule. Also called "prepayment fee", "early payoff penalty", "exit fee". Examples: "Mortgage repayment earlyPrepaymentPenalty '$500'", "Loan agreement earlyPrepaymentPenalty '2% of remaining balance'", "Car loan earlyPrepaymentPenalty '$100'".

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: targetCollection
candidates.comment: A specific collection relation between an update action and the collection of things that is the target of the action. Also called "collection to update", "target set", "destination collection". Examples: "The add action has targetCollection a list of items", "The update action's targetCollection is a database table", "This action modifies a targetCollection of documents.". Distinct from object, which is a more general target of an action.

candidates.label: contraindication
candidates.comment: A medical restriction relation for a medical device or therapy, indicating a contraindication. Also called "medical warning", "precaution", "not recommended for". Examples: "Drug therapy contraindication 'Pregnancy'", "Medical device contraindication 'Pacemaker users'".

candidates.label: collection
candidates.comment: A target relation for an update action, indicating the collection that is being updated. Also called "target collection", "updated collection", "collection object". Examples: "Add item update action collection 'Shopping Cart'", "Remove item update action collection 'Wishlist'".

candidates.label: suggestedAge
candidates.comment: A quantitative value indicating the recommended age or age range for an intended audience or person. Also called "recommended age", "age range", "target age", "suitable age". Examples: "The toy has suggestedAge 3-5 years", "The audience specification includes suggestedAge 18+", "This product is for suggestedAge 6-12 months.". Distinct from suggestedMinAge and suggestedMaxAge, which specify only the minimum or maximum.

candidates.label: requiredGender
candidates.comment: A required gender relation between a people audience and the specific gender criteria for inclusion. Also called target gender, gender requirement. Examples: "An event targets a people audience with required gender 'female'.", "A survey specifies a required gender 'male'.", "A product is marketed to a people audience with required gender 'unspecified'."

candidates.label: targetDescription
candidates.comment: A textual description of a node within an established educational framework. Also called "framework node description", "educational standard description", "learning objective description". Examples: "The alignment object has targetDescription 'Understand basic algebra'", "The educational framework node's targetDescription explains the competency", "This targetDescription details a specific learning outcome."

candidates.label: paymentDue
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the date and time by which payment for an invoice or order is required. Also called due date, payment deadline, payment required by. Examples: An invoice has a payment due date of '2023-12-31T23:59:59'. An order has a payment due date of '2024-01-15'. The bill has a payment due date of 'next Friday'. Distinct from paymentDueDate, which is specifically a Date, not DateTime.

relations.definition: Indicates the authority that enforces a penalty or obligation.
relations.embedding_query_text: imposed_by: Indicates the authority that enforces a penalty or obligation.

Fine for Play Store rules -> European Commission

chosen_property.label: imposedBy
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the authority that imposes a penalty or obligation.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property fits; minting new property.

candidates.label: referee
candidates.comment: A referee relation between a sports event and the person officiating it to enforce rules. Also called officiated by, umpire, judge. Examples: "A football match has a referee 'Pierluigi Collina'.", "A tennis match has a referee 'Eva Asderaki-Moore'.", "A basketball game has a referee 'Joey Crawford'."

candidates.label: legislationPassedBy
candidates.comment: A passing authority relation between a piece of legislation and the organization or person that originally enacted it. Also called: enacted by, made by, legislated by. Examples: "Primary Legislation legislationPassedBy Parliament", "Secondary Legislation legislationPassedBy Government", "Local Bylaw legislationPassedBy City Council". Distinct from legislationResponsible, which refers to the ministry or individual in charge of elaborating or addressing questions about the legislation.

candidates.label: issuedBy
candidates.comment: An issuing authority relation between a certification, permit, or ticket and the organization that granted or provided it. Also called granted by, provided by, authorized by, issuer. Examples: A driver's license is issuedBy 'Department of Motor Vehicles'. A concert ticket is issuedBy 'Ticketmaster'. A professional certification is issuedBy 'Certification Body X'.

candidates.label: legislationEnsuresImplementationOf
candidates.comment: An implementation assurance relation between two pieces of legislation, where one ensures the implementation of the other by modifying national laws. Also called: implements, ensures compliance with, enforces. Examples: "National Law A legislationEnsuresImplementationOf EU Regulation B", "State Statute legislationEnsuresImplementationOf Federal Act", "Local Ordinance legislationEnsuresImplementationOf Regional Directive". Distinct from legislationTransposes, which specifically refers to fulfilling objectives by passing implementation measures.

candidates.label: earlyPrepaymentPenalty
candidates.comment: An early prepayment penalty relation between a repayment specification and a monetary amount, representing the fee for paying off a loan ahead of schedule. Also called "prepayment fee", "early payoff penalty", "exit fee". Examples: "Mortgage repayment earlyPrepaymentPenalty '$500'", "Loan agreement earlyPrepaymentPenalty '2% of remaining balance'", "Car loan earlyPrepaymentPenalty '$100'".

candidates.label: contraindication
candidates.comment: A medical restriction relation for a medical device or therapy, indicating a contraindication. Also called "medical warning", "precaution", "not recommended for". Examples: "Drug therapy contraindication 'Pregnancy'", "Medical device contraindication 'Pacemaker users'".

candidates.label: legislationCountersignedBy
candidates.comment: A countersignature relation between a piece of legislation and the person or organization that countersigned it. Also called: countersigned by, officially endorsed by, co-signed by. Examples: "The Bill of Rights legislationCountersignedBy President Washington", "EU Directive 2023/45 legislationCountersignedBy European Commission", "Local Ordinance legislationCountersignedBy City Clerk".

candidates.label: legislationResponsible
candidates.comment: A responsibility relation between a piece of legislation and the individual or organization accountable for its elaboration or inquiries. Also called: responsible for, overseen by, managed by. Examples: "Health Act legislationResponsible Ministry of Health", "Environmental Law legislationResponsible EPA", "Tax Reform legislationResponsible Treasury Department". Distinct from legislationPassedBy, which refers to the original enacting authority.

candidates.label: jurisdiction
candidates.comment: A legal scope relation between a government service or legislation and the administrative area or territory where it applies. Also called legal authority, governing area, applicable region, domain of law. Examples: A government service has a jurisdiction of 'California'. Legislation has a jurisdiction of 'United States federal law'. A permit applies to the jurisdiction of 'City of London'. Distinct from eligibleRegion or ineligibleRegion, which are about availability, not legal authority.

candidates.label: legalRepresentative
candidates.comment: A legal representation relation between an organization and the person(s) authorized to act on its behalf in legal matters. Also called authorized representative, legal agent, official representative, corporate officer. Examples: An organization has a legalRepresentative of 'its CEO'. A company's legalRepresentative is 'its sole administrator'. The board appointed 'Jane Doe' as legalRepresentative. Distinct from employee, which is a general employment relation, not specifically legal representation.

relations.definition: Specifies the quantity or value associated with an action.
relations.embedding_query_text: amount: Specifies the quantity or value associated with an action.

chosen_property.label: amount
chosen_property.justification: Candidate 'amount' matches the relation and signature.

candidates.label: amount
candidates.comment: An amount relation between a financial entity (e.g., loan, grant, money transfer) and the monetary value or number associated with it. Also called value, sum, quantity of money. Examples: "A loan's amount is '$10,000'.", "The grant's amount is '€5,000'.", "A money transfer's amount is '250'."

candidates.label: amountOfThisGood
candidates.comment: An amount of this good relation between a type and quantity node and the numerical quantity of a specific good included in an offer. Also called quantity, number of items, item count. Examples: "A shopping cart item's amount of this good is '2'.", "The offer specifies an amount of this good as '5'."

candidates.label: value
candidates.comment: A value relation between a monetary amount, property value, or quantitative value and its specific numerical, textual, boolean, or structured content. Also called amount, quantity, content. Examples: "QuantitativeValue value '10'", "PropertyValue value 'red'", "MonetaryAmount value '99.99'".

candidates.label: requiredQuantity
candidates.comment: A required quantity relation between a how-to item and the amount of that item needed. Also called quantity needed, amount required. Examples: "A how-to item 'sugar' has a required quantity '1 cup'.", "A crafting project needs a required quantity '5 sheets of paper'.", "A recipe step specifies a required quantity '2 eggs'."

candidates.label: referenceQuantity
candidates.comment: A reference quantity relation between a unit price specification and the specific quantity for which the stated price applies. Also called quantity for price, price per quantity. Examples: "A electricity price specification has a reference quantity '4 kWh'.", "A bulk discount has a reference quantity '10 units'.", "A service charge has a reference quantity '1 hour'."

candidates.label: eligibleQuantity
candidates.comment: An eligible quantity relation between a demand, offer, or price specification and the quantitative value representing the ordering quantities for which it is valid. Also called "valid quantity range", "order quantity limit", "bulk discount quantity". Examples: "Offer 'Bulk Discount' eligibleQuantity 'Minimum 10 units'", "Price specification eligibleQuantity '5-100 items'", "Shipping charge eligibleQuantity 'Over 50 kg'".

candidates.label: orderQuantity
candidates.comment: The number or quantity of a specific item ordered within an order item. Also called item quantity, ordered amount, number of units. Examples: "OrderItem A orderQuantity 2", "OrderItem B orderQuantity 5", "OrderItem C orderQuantity 1". Distinct from numItems (for ShippingConditions), which is a limit on total items for shipping.

candidates.label: price
candidates.comment: A financial attribute indicating the monetary value of an offer, product, or price component. Also called cost, rate, charge, amount. Examples: An offer has a price of '19.99'. A product has a price of '100'. The service has a price of '50.00'. Distinct from priceCurrency, which specifies the currency of the price.

candidates.label: yield
candidates.comment: A yield relation between a how-to guide and a quantitative value or text, specifying the quantity or type of output produced by following the instructions. Also called output quantity, resulting amount, production yield. Examples: HowToRecipe yield "12 cookies", HowToCraft yield "1 paper airplane", HowToGuide yield "5 liters of jam".

candidates.label: billingIncrement
candidates.comment: A number specifying the minimal quantity and rounding increment for billing. Also called: billing unit, minimum billing quantity. Examples: "UnitPriceSpecification 'Data Usage' billingIncrement '1' (GB)", "UnitPriceSpecification 'Consulting' billingIncrement '0.25' (hours)."

relations.definition: Indicates the cause or justification for an action.
relations.embedding_query_text: reason: Indicates the cause or justification for an action.

instances: Fine for Play Store rules -> Google Play

chosen_property.label: reason
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the cause or justification for an action.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property expresses the reason for an action; minting new property.

candidates.label: error
candidates.comment: An error relation between a failed action and the thing providing more information on the cause of the failure. Also called "failure cause", "problem details", "issue description". Examples: "Action 'Payment' error 'Insufficient Funds'", "Action 'Login' error 'Invalid Credentials'", "Action 'File Upload' error 'File Too Large'". Distinct from errorCode, which is a specific code for the error.

candidates.label: ratingExplanation
candidates.comment: A rating explanation relation between a rating and a brief text providing context or justification for the rating. Also called rating justification, explanation for rating, rating context. Examples: "A product rating includes a rating explanation 'The battery life was excellent, but the camera was disappointing'.", "A fact-check rating has a rating explanation 'The claim was partially true, lacking full context'.", "A service rating has a rating explanation 'The staff were friendly, but wait times were long'."

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: potentialAction
candidates.comment: A behavioral attribute indicating an idealized action in which a thing could potentially serve as the object. Also called possible action, available action, actionable item. Examples: A product has a potential action 'BuyAction'. A book has a potential action 'ReadAction'. A movie has a potential action 'WatchAction'.

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: actionStatus
candidates.comment: An action status relation between an action and its current disposition or state. Also called action state, status of action, disposition. Examples: "A 'purchase' action's action status is 'CompletedActionStatus'.", "A 'shipment' action's action status is 'PotentialActionStatus'."

candidates.label: answerExplanation
candidates.comment: An answer explanation relation between an answer and a comment or web content providing a detailed clarification or step-by-step reasoning. Also called solution explanation, answer justification, detailed response. Examples: "An answer's answer explanation details the calculation steps.", "The correct answer's explanation clarifies the underlying principle."

candidates.label: result
candidates.comment: The outcome or product generated by an action. Also called outcome, product, output, consequence. Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: actionAccessibilityRequirement
candidates.comment: An action accessibility requirement relation between a consume action and the specifications that must be met to perform it. Also called action prerequisites, access conditions, fulfillment requirements. Examples: "A 'watch movie' action's accessibility requirement is 'subscription'.", "A 'download software' action's accessibility requirement is 'login'."

relations.definition: Indicates that one thing is a component of another.
relations.embedding_query_text: part_of: Indicates that one thing is a component of another.

instances: First DMA action -> EU fines Google
Fine for search favouritism -> EU fines Google
Fine for Play Store rules -> EU fines Google

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: isPartOfBioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A biochemical part-whole relation indicating that one biochemical entity is a component of another larger biochemical entity. Also called component of biochem entity, contained within biochem entity, element of biochem entity. Examples: A protein domain isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a larger protein'. A subunit isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a protein complex'. A specific gene sequence isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a chromosome'.

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: partOfSystem
candidates.comment: A biological relation between an anatomical structure and the anatomical or organ system it is a component of. Also called is a component of, belongs to, is found in, forms part of. Examples: The heart is part of the circulatory system. The lungs are part of the respiratory system. A bone is part of the skeletal system.

candidates.label: ingredients
candidates.comment: A component relation between a recipe and the individual food items or substances required for its preparation. Also called components, recipe items, constituents, elements. Examples: A cake recipe lists 'flour' as an ingredient. A soup recipe lists 'carrots' as an ingredient. A cocktail recipe lists 'gin' as an ingredient.

candidates.label: subEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger event and a smaller event that is a component or part of it. Also called "part of event", "component event", "nested event", "event within event". Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". Distinct from superEvent, which points from the smaller event to the larger one.

candidates.label: hasBioChemEntityPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a biochemical entity and one of its constituent biochemical entities. Also called composed of, contains, includes part, made of. Examples: "A protein has a BioChemEntity part of an amino acid sequence.", "A cell has BioChemEntity parts like organelles.", "A molecule has BioChemEntity parts of atoms."

candidates.label: subStructure
candidates.comment: A component relation between an anatomical structure and the smaller anatomical structures that comprise it. Also called "component structure", "anatomical part", "composed of", "contains structure". Examples: "The heart has subStructure atria", "The brain's subStructure includes the cerebrum", "This anatomical structure is made up of several subStructure elements."

candidates.label: subEvents
candidates.comment: A collection of hierarchical relations between a larger event and multiple smaller events that are components or parts of it. Also called "component events", "nested events", "events within event", "parts of event". Examples: "The conference has subEvents multiple presentations", "The festival's subEvents include several concerts and workshops", "This event comprises many subEvents.". Distinct from subEvent, which refers to a single component event.

candidates.label: parentItem
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a discussion item and its preceding item or a creative work it comments on. Also called part of, replies to, refers to, is a response to. Examples: A comment is a parent item of another comment. A question is a parent item of an answer. An answer is a parent item of a follow-up comment. Distinct from comment, which points from something to a comment about it.

relations.definition: Indicates the legal framework governing an action.
relations.embedding_query_text: under_law: Indicates the legal framework governing an action.

instances: First DMA action -> Digital Markets Act

chosen_property.label: underLaw
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the legal framework governing an action.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property expresses being governed by a law; minting new property.

candidates.label: jurisdiction
candidates.comment: A legal scope relation between a government service or legislation and the administrative area or territory where it applies. Also called legal authority, governing area, applicable region, domain of law. Examples: A government service has a jurisdiction of 'California'. Legislation has a jurisdiction of 'United States federal law'. A permit applies to the jurisdiction of 'City of London'. Distinct from eligibleRegion or ineligibleRegion, which are about availability, not legal authority.

candidates.label: legislationApplies
candidates.comment: An informative legislative transfer relation indicating that a piece of legislation incorporates or references another legislation within a different legal context, without legal binding. Also called incorporates legislation, references law, applies provisions of, draws from legislation. Examples: A national law legislationApplies 'a European Directive'. A local ordinance legislationApplies 'state regulations'. This consolidated law legislationApplies 'the original act'. Distinct from legislationTransposes, which implies a legally binding transposition.

candidates.label: legislationJurisdiction
candidates.comment: A jurisdiction relation between a piece of legislation and the administrative area from which it originates. Also called: originating jurisdiction, legal territory, governing region. Examples: "Federal Law legislationJurisdiction United States", "State Statute legislationJurisdiction California", "EU Directive legislationJurisdiction European Union".

candidates.label: actionStatus
candidates.comment: An action status relation between an action and its current disposition or state. Also called action state, status of action, disposition. Examples: "A 'purchase' action's action status is 'CompletedActionStatus'.", "A 'shipment' action's action status is 'PotentialActionStatus'."

candidates.label: potentialAction
candidates.comment: A behavioral attribute indicating an idealized action in which a thing could potentially serve as the object. Also called possible action, available action, actionable item. Examples: A product has a potential action 'BuyAction'. A book has a potential action 'ReadAction'. A movie has a potential action 'WatchAction'.

candidates.label: legislationCommences
candidates.comment: A legislative activation relation between a piece of legislation and another legislation that it brings into legal effect. Also called brings into force, enacts, activates law, sets into effect. Examples: Legislation A legislationCommences 'Legislation B'. The enabling act legislationCommences 'the new regulations'. This decree legislationCommences 'the policy changes'.

candidates.label: legislationLegalForce
candidates.comment: A legal force status relation between a piece of legislation and its current state of being in force. Also called: force status, legal validity, in effect status. Examples: "New Act legislationLegalForce InForce", "Old Regulation legislationLegalForce NotInForce", "Partial Amendment legislationLegalForce PartiallyInForce".

candidates.label: legislationEnsuresImplementationOf
candidates.comment: An implementation assurance relation between two pieces of legislation, where one ensures the implementation of the other by modifying national laws. Also called: implements, ensures compliance with, enforces. Examples: "National Law A legislationEnsuresImplementationOf EU Regulation B", "State Statute legislationEnsuresImplementationOf Federal Act", "Local Ordinance legislationEnsuresImplementationOf Regional Directive". Distinct from legislationTransposes, which specifically refers to fulfilling objectives by passing implementation measures.

candidates.label: legislationType
candidates.comment: A type relation between a piece of legislation and its classification (e.g., law, act, directive). Also called: legislative type, legal category, form of law. Examples: "GDPR legislationType regulation", "Civil Rights Act legislationType law", "EU Directive legislationType directive".

candidates.label: legislationTransposes
candidates.comment: A transposition relation between two pieces of legislation, where one fulfills the objectives of the other through implementation measures. Also called: transposes, implements directive, fulfills objectives of. Examples: "Member State Law legislationTransposes EU Directive", "Regional Act legislationTransposes National Regulation", "Local Ordinance legislationTransposes State Mandate". Distinct from legislationEnsuresImplementationOf, which implies modifying national legislations to avoid contradiction, rather than fulfilling objectives.

relations.definition: Indicates that one event occurs after another.
relations.embedding_query_text: follows: Indicates that one event occurs after another.

instances: Google must comply -> EU fines Google

chosen_property.label: follows
chosen_property.definition: Indicates that one event or mission follows another in sequence.
chosen_property.justification: Candidate 'follows' matches the temporal sequence relation.

candidates.label: follows
candidates.comment: A follows relation representing a generic uni-directional social connection between two people. Also called: is following, subscribes to, tracks. Examples: "Alice follows Bob", "Charlie follows David", "Eve follows Frank". Distinct from followee, which is the object of a follow action.

candidates.label: previousItem
candidates.comment: A sequential relation between a list item and the list item that immediately precedes it. Also called precedes, comes after, follows. Examples: List item 'B' has a previous item 'A'. The current item's previous item is the one before it. In a breadcrumb trail, the current page has a previous item. Distinct from nextItem, which links to the item that follows.

candidates.label: eventAttendanceMode
candidates.comment: An event attendance mode relation between an event and the enumeration indicating whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix. Also called "attendance format", "event delivery mode", "participation mode". Examples: "Event 'Conference' eventAttendanceMode 'OnlineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Workshop' eventAttendanceMode 'OfflineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Hybrid Meeting' eventAttendanceMode 'MixedEventAttendanceMode'".

candidates.label: followup
candidates.comment: A followup relation between a medical procedure and the typical or recommended post-procedure care. Also called: aftercare, post-procedure care, follow-up instructions. Examples: "Surgery" followup "Rest for 2 weeks, avoid heavy lifting", "Dental Cleaning" followup "Brush twice daily, floss regularly", "Vaccination" followup "Monitor for side effects, schedule booster shot".

candidates.label: afterMedia
candidates.comment: An after media relation between a how-to direction and a media object or URL depicting the state or circumstances after completing that step. Also called post-step media, result image, outcome visual. Examples: "A recipe direction's after media is an image of the mixed ingredients.", "The assembly instruction's after media is a video of the connected parts."

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: repeatCount
candidates.comment: A repeat count relation between a schedule and the total number of times a recurring event will occur. Also called number of repetitions, event occurrences. Examples: "A weekly meeting schedule has a repeat count of 10.", "A training course schedule has a repeat count of 5.", "A daily alarm schedule has a repeat count of 365."

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

relations.definition: Indicates the entity that is the focus of an action.
relations.embedding_query_text: subject: Indicates the entity that is the focus of an action.

chosen_property.label: about
chosen_property.justification: Candidate 'about' expresses the subject matter relation.

candidates.label: studySubject
candidates.comment: An investigative relation between a medical study and the medical entity (condition, therapy, drug, etc.) that is being investigated. Also called "subject of investigation", "research focus", "entity studied", "trial subject". Examples: "The medical study has studySubject a new drug", "The clinical trial's studySubject is a specific medical condition", "This study investigates a studySubject therapy."

candidates.label: mainEntity
candidates.comment: A main entity relation between a creative work and the primary entity it describes. Also called: primary subject, about entity, central topic. Examples: "Wikipedia Article mainEntity Albert Einstein", "News Report mainEntity The Election", "Research Paper mainEntity Quantum Physics". Distinct from mainEntityOfPage, which indicates the page for which this thing is the main entity.

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: guidelineSubject
candidates.comment: A guideline subject relation between a medical guideline and the medical conditions, treatments, or other entities it addresses. Also called: guideline topic, subject matter, focus. Examples: "AHA Guideline for Hypertension" guideline subject "Hypertension", "NICE Guideline for Diabetes" guideline subject "Type 2 Diabetes", "WHO COVID-19 Guidelines" guideline subject "COVID-19". Distinct from guideline, which is the guideline itself.

candidates.label: followee
candidates.comment: A followee relation between a follow action and the person or organization that is being followed. Also called: followed entity, subject of follow, target of follow. Examples: "User A follows User B" followee "User B", "Fan follows Band X" followee "Band X", "Journalist follows News Organization Y" followee "News Organization Y". Distinct from follows, which is the general social relation.

candidates.label: spatialCoverage
candidates.comment: A geographic focus relation between a creative work and the place(s) that are the primary subject or focus of its content. Also called "geographic scope", "covered area", "location focus", "content location". Examples: "A weather dataset has spatialCoverage New York State", "The historical map's spatialCoverage is ancient Rome", "This research paper's spatialCoverage is the Arctic region.". Distinct from nextItem, which links to the item that follows.

candidates.label: numberOfPreviousOwners
candidates.comment: The total number of previous owners of a vehicle, including the current owner. Also called prior owners, owner history count, past owners. Examples: "Used Car A numberOfPreviousOwners 1", "Vintage Vehicle B numberOfPreviousOwners 3", "New Car C numberOfPreviousOwners 0".

candidates.label: beforeMedia
candidates.comment: A media object representing the circumstances prior to performing a how-to direction. Also called: pre-action media, initial state media. Examples: "HowToDirection 'Install Shelf' beforeMedia 'Image of empty wall'", "HowToDirection 'Bake Cake' beforeMedia 'Video of ingredients on counter'."

candidates.label: paymentDue
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the date and time by which payment for an invoice or order is required. Also called due date, payment deadline, payment required by. Examples: An invoice has a payment due date of '2023-12-31T23:59:59'. An order has a payment due date of '2024-01-15'. The bill has a payment due date of 'next Friday'. Distinct from paymentDueDate, which is specifically a Date, not DateTime.

candidates.label: paymentDueDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the date by which payment for an invoice or order is required. Also called due date, payment deadline, payment required by. Examples: An invoice has a payment due date of '2023-12-31'. An order has a payment due date of '2024-01-15'. The bill has a payment due date of '2024-02-28'. Distinct from paymentDue, which can include time information.

candidates.label: customerRemorseReturnFees
candidates.comment: A return policy relation between a merchant return policy and the type of fees applied when a product is returned due to customer remorse. Also called: remorse return fees, change-of-mind return fees, customer-initiated return charges. Examples: "Electronics Store" customer remorse return fees "ReturnShippingFees", "Clothing Retailer" customer remorse return fees "RestockingFee", "Bookstore" customer remorse return fees "NoFees".

candidates.label: contraindication
candidates.comment: A medical restriction relation for a medical device or therapy, indicating a contraindication. Also called "medical warning", "precaution", "not recommended for". Examples: "Drug therapy contraindication 'Pregnancy'", "Medical device contraindication 'Pacemaker users'".

candidates.label: dateVehicleFirstRegistered
candidates.comment: A temporal registration relation between a vehicle and the date of its first registration with public authorities. Also called: first registration date, initial registration, vehicle registration date. Examples: "Car" date vehicle first registered "2018-03-15", "Motorcycle" date vehicle first registered "2020-07-01", "Truck" date vehicle first registered "2015-11-20".
